---
title: "DataCleaningProject"
format: pdf
---
I extracted 5 users from the Enron Email Dataset created by CMU. Here is the link: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~enron/.

```{r}
#Part 1: find every email file
people <- c("allen-p", "arnold-j", "arora-h", "badeer-r", "bailey-s")
pat    <- paste(people, collapse = "|")

files <- list.files(".", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
files <- files[grepl(paste0("/(", pat, ")/"), files)]
length(files)

#Part 2- read the header of one email
read_email <- function(path) {
  lines <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE, encoding = "latin1")

  blank <- which(trimws(lines) == "")[1]
  if (is.na(blank)) blank <- length(lines) + 1
  head <- paste(lines[seq_len(blank - 1)], collapse = "\n")

  #Wrap onto new lines starting with a space/tab
  head <- gsub("\n[ \t]+", " ", head)
  head <- strsplit(head, "\n")[[1]]

  #returns the text after "To:"
  grab <- function(name) {
    hit <- grep(paste0("^", name, ":"), head, value = TRUE)[1]
    sub(paste0("^", name, ":[ ]*"), "", hit)
  }

  data.frame(file = path,
             from = grab("From"), to = grab("To"), cc = grab("Cc"),
             subject = grab("Subject"), date = grab("Date"),
             x_from = grab("X-From"), x_folder = grab("X-Folder"),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

#Part 3- read all emails into one table
emails <- do.call(rbind, lapply(files, read_email))
emails$id      <- seq_len(nrow(emails))
emails$mailbox <- sub(paste0(".*/(", pat, ")/.*"), "\\1", emails$file)
emails$folder  <- sub(paste0(".*/(?:", pat, ")/([^/]+)/.*"), "\\1", emails$file, perl = TRUE)

#Part 4- make all missing values look the same
#some headers are absent (NA) and some are present but blank
emails[] <- lapply(emails, function(x) ifelse(trimws(x) == "", NA, x))
colSums(is.na(emails))   # how much is missing in each column

#clean up sender names
# "Arora, Harry </O=ENRON/...>"  and  "Harry Arora"  to "harry arora"
clean_name <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub('"', "", x)
  x <- sub("\\s*<.*$", "", x)#drop <...> part
  x <- trimws(x)
  x <- ifelse(grepl(",", x), sub("^(.*),\\s*(.*)$", "\\2 \\1", x), x)
  tolower(x)
}
emails$sender_name <- clean_name(emails$x_from)
emails$from        <- tolower(emails$from)

#Part 5-fix dates
# "Tue, 4 Dec 2001 10:30:17 -0800 (PST)" to 2001-12-04
emails$date_clean <- as.Date(sub("^[A-Za-z]+, ", "", emails$date), format = "%d %b %Y")

#Part6- one row per recipientt
recipients <- strsplit(emails$to, ",\\s*")
recipients_long <- data.frame(
  id        = rep(emails$id, lengths(recipients)),
  recipient = tolower(trimws(unlist(recipients))),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
nrow(recipients_long)

#Part 7- handle impossible dates
sum(emails$date_clean < as.Date("1999-01-01"), na.rm = TRUE)   # how many
emails$date_clean[which(emails$date_clean < as.Date("1999-01-01"))] <- NA

#Part 8- sort and save
emails <- emails[order(emails$date_clean), ]
write.csv(emails,          "emails_clean.csv",     row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(recipients_long, "recipients_long.csv",  row.names = FALSE)

head(emails[, c("mailbox", "folder", "sender_name", "subject", "date_clean")])

#barplot
barplot(table(format(emails$date_clean, "%Y")), main = "Emails per year")
```
